title: First 14-Day Entitlement and Remediation Runbook for Enterprise Go-Live
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:

This runbook defines the operational checklist, entitlement validation, telemetry assertions, and remediation steps for the first 14 calendar days after an enterprise tenant goes live with Redwood. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), and oncall SRE/Platform engineers supporting dedicated and private deployments.

Purpose and scope:
- Ensure contractual entitlements and configuration match production behavior (rate limits, reserved capacity, feature flags).
- Verify baseline performance, cost signals, and functional correctness across the tenant surface (ingress, model routing, responses).
- Provide clear, actionable remediation steps for common failure modes observed during early adoption.
- Standardize communication templates for customer updates and internal escalation.

Quick reference SLOs to validate (tenant-visible):
- Token generation latency: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 400ms (hosted); for Dedicated SLA values negotiated per contract.
- Request success rate: >= 99.5% (5xx + client-error excluding rate-limit).
- Input-to-output throughput: within +/-25% of capacity reservation in first 14 days.
- Cost anomaly guardrail: daily spend drift <= 30% vs baseline estimate.

Prerequisites (pre-go-live verification):
1) Entitlement manifest uploaded to tenant account and validated (rate limits, model access, quota tiers).
2) Telemetry gatekeeper integration completed and test events flowing to telemetry index (tenant-metrics-collector).
3) Ingress and egress firewalls or peering verified (for Private deployments).
4) Canary traffic and synthetic journeys executed with pass criteria met (see Acceptance criteria).

Roles & ownership:
- Customer Success Lead: primary contact for customer communication and business escalation.
- Solutions Engineer: owns configuration validation, post-provision tuning, and acceptance tests.
- SRE oncall: owns production remediation activities, service-level alerts, and rollbacks.
- Model Ops: validates model correctness, quality drift, and rollout adjustments.

Entitlement and configuration validation checklist (first 48 hours):
1) Confirm rate-limiting policy applied to tenant: run endpoint check against /v1/usage/limits and compare to contract.
2) Validate model catalog access: attempt to instantiate the tenant-default model with SDK key and ensure model-router returns expected model hash.
3) Verify reserved capacity is reachable: confirm at least one GPU pool connection is established (service: gpu-allocator).
4) Confirm data plane encryption and KMS key access (for Private): kms: TestEncrypt API returns 200.
5) Check billing tags and cost attribution metadata are attached to tenant requests.

Telemetry assertions (queries and thresholds to run daily):
- Request success rate (PromQL):
  sum(rate(redwood_api_requests_total{tenant="TENANT_ID",code!~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_api_requests_total{tenant="TENANT_ID"}[5m])) > 0.995

- Request latency (p95):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant="TENANT_ID"}[5m])) by (le)) < 0.4

- Token cost per 1k tokens (derived): daily_token_cost = sum(token_cost_daily{tenant="TENANT_ID"}) / (sum(tokens_generated_daily{tenant="TENANT_ID"})/1000)
  Alert if daily_token_cost > expected_unit_cost * 1.5

- Synthetic journey success (example curl):
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TENANT_KEY}" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-7b", "input":"The capital of France is"}'
  Expected: 200, contains "Paris" or equivalent.

Acceptance criteria for steady state (end of day 14):
- All telemetry assertions pass for at least 72% of 12-hour windows during day 8–14.
- No more than two major incidents attributable to platform plumbing (networking, quota enforcement, ingress) during first 14 days.
- Customer-specified quality regression tests (prompt-set) maintain >= 90% pass rate versus baseline.

Runbook: top-level remediation flows (ordered by likelihood)

1) High error rate (5xx spikes)
- Observable signals: 5xx spike in redwood_api_requests_total, sudden p95 latency surge, GPU pool utilization near 100%.
- Immediate steps (SRE oncall):
  a) Silence non-actionable alerts and annotate incident channel (#cs-tenant-TENANTID) with initial findings.
  b) Check gpu-allocator and model-router health: kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=gpu-allocator; kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=model-router\  c) If GPU pool OOMs or ejects pods, remove tenant from routing (via control plane: POST /admin/route/remove-tenant) and failover to a compatible fallback model (see control-plane runbook snippet).
  d) If ingress NLB shows connection errors, run tcpdump on ingress gateway and escalate to network team.
- Customer comms template: "We've detected elevated error rates affecting your tenant. We've removed traffic from the impacted pool while we investigate; your traffic is being routed to a fallback model to preserve availability. Expected ETA: 30–90 minutes."

2) Latency regressions with normal error rate
- Signals: p95 latency increased > 2x baseline while success rate remains > 99%.
- Remediation (SE + SRE):
  a) Check continuous batching and KV cache hit rate stats: query tenant_kvcache_hit_ratio{tenant="TENANT_ID"}[10m]
  b) If cache miss spike: warm cache by replaying synthetic prefix requests (see synthetic warmup script below).
  c) If batching latency high: adjust max_batch_size for tenant via tenant config API and schedule a controlled scaling of worker replicas.

Synthetic warmup script (example):
```
for i in {1..100}; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TENANT_KEY}" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"model":"tenant-default","input":"Warmup prompt '$i'"}' >/dev/null &
done
wait
```

3) Unexpected quality regressions (model output accuracy or hallucinations)
- Signals: customer report, failing prompt-set evals, sudden divergence in evaluation scores in eval-harness.
- Remediation (Model Ops + SE):
  a) Re-run prompt-set locally against model hash reported in runtime logs.
  b) If regression confirmed, initiate model rollback to prior model hash using the rollout API and notify customer.
  c) Open a model-regression ticket with Research with full prompt-set + failure examples.

4) Cost surge (unexpected spend)
- Signals: daily_token_cost spike, unexpected embedding indexing runs, long-running batch jobs attributed to tenant.
- Remediation (CS + FinOps + SE):
  a) Temporarily restrict tenant concurrency or reduce max_tokens and max_concurrent requests via entitlement config.
  b) If chargeback rules apply, create a cost hold and notify billing.
  c) Analyze request traces to identify runaway loops or bots. Provide sample request IDs to customer.

Escalation matrix (when to escalate to engineering and execs):
- Level 1 (CS + SE): service-impacting but contained, ETA < 4 hours.
- Level 2 (SRE + Model Ops): multi-region impact or stuck routing, ETA < 8 hours.
- Level 3 (VP-eng + Legal + Customer Exec): prolonged outage > 8 hours, data exposure, contract breach risk.

Internal communication templates (use in incident channel and customer emails):
- Initial: "We have observed an operational issue affecting your service. We are investigating and have put temporary mitigations in place. We will provide an update within 30 minutes."
- Update: "Root cause update: [summary]. Current impact: [number of affected requests / %]. Next action: [action]. ETA: [time window]."
- Resolution: "The issue is resolved. Root cause: [summary]. Remediation steps taken: [list]. Postmortem ETA: [date/time]."

Checklist: daily run cadence (days 0–14):
- Day 0–2: entitlement checks, basic telemetry smoke tests, synthetic journeys every 2 hours, billing tag verification.
- Day 3–7: add expanded prompt-set runs, monitor for anomalies in quality and cost, weekly SE tuning session.
- Day 8–14: stability acceptance tests, QBR prep package assembled for customer (see QBR signals below).

QBR signals to prepare for week 2 review (deliverable list):
- Telemetry summary: request volume, latency curves (p50/p95), error rate, token cost per 1k tokens.
- Prompt-set evaluation results (pass/fail counts and examples).
- Entitlement verification report (actual vs contracted limits).
- Incidents and remediation log (timeline, impact, and customer-facing notes).
- Recommended changes: capacity, batching, or model variant suggestions.

Related runbooks & links:
- tenant-observability-contract-lifecycle (link internal)
- canary-simulation-and-auto-alert-playbook (link internal)
- model-switchover-fallback-triage-runbook (link internal)

Appendix: common commands and API snippets
- Validate entitlement API:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_KEY}" https://controlplane.redwood.internal/v1/tenants/TENANT_ID/entitlements

- Remove tenant from pool (control-plane):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_KEY}" -d '{"tenant":"TENANT_ID","action":"remove_from_pool"}' https://controlplane.redwood.internal/v1/admin/route

- Rollback model (example):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_KEY}" -d '{"tenant":"TENANT_ID","route":"default","model_hash":"<previous_hash>"}' https://controlplane.redwood.internal/v1/admin/rollout

Concluding notes:
This runbook is iterative. During onboarding of new enterprise tenants, please capture any new failure modes in the ticket stub below and propose additions to this document. Maintain a record of all customer-facing messages in the tenant's go-live folder for audit and QBR preparation.

Audit ticket stub (copy into JIRA/Ticket):
- Tenant: TENANT_ID
- Onboarded by: <CS lead>
- Start date: <YYYY-MM-DD>
- Key incidents (summary, timestamps, owner)
- Actions taken and follow-ups
- Postmortem link (if applicable)
